task: Find why project-mode moss check rejected `echo v` for a Vector that standalone check accepted (P25-S-ARCH-019).
observation: The two check modes did not run the same pipeline. Standalone check ran Parser, Checker, and FunctionalOptimizer. Project check called analyze_project_sources, which also ran Generator::generate() and discarded the Rust. So any native-lowering CompileError, here NATIVE_ECHO_DISPLAY_UNSUPPORTED from the Echo lowering, became a project-only check verdict. The diagnostic code gave no sign that it came from the backend rather than the checker.
impact: An agent relying on `moss check --json` got a different answer for the same source depending on whether a Moss.toml was nearby. Moving the display rule into the checker alone would not have closed the class: any later lowering-only diagnostic would diverge again.
evidence: src/moss.cpp analyze_project_sources at c2e106c (Generator(...).generate() at line 30461, called from the check path at line 36289)

resolution.summary: Project check and semantic queries now use check_project_semantics (checker plus functional optimizer, no lowering), matching standalone check; the echo display rule is a checker rule (ECHO_DISPLAY_UNSUPPORTED).

task: Make sure the new ECHO_DISPLAY_UNSUPPORTED checker rule neither pre-empts pinned diagnostics nor rejects valid code.
observation: Two tools caught three problems before any commit. The first was a repository-wide ok/not-ok diff of `moss check --json` over all 1,876 tracked .moss files, comparing the c2e106c baseline with the new compiler. The second ran every tests/run.sh reject_case expectation directly. The first draft of the rule changed 4 extra verdicts. Two pinned negatives (functional_placeholder_noncopy_field and functional_placeholder_noncopy_identity) reported the echo error instead of their FUNCTIONAL_SEMANTIC_ERROR, because the type walk reaches `echo` before the ownership walk. The Phase 20 probe guard_range_binary_echo, whose FileIO Range has a deliberate binary-safe Display, was also rejected. So was the IDE fixture phase225_pipeline_completion.
impact: Without the scan, make check would have failed late in tests/run.sh, or a documented Phase 20 behaviour would have been removed silently. The fix was to defer the display error to the end of Checker::run, keep FileIO Range displayable as a scalar, and update the one fixture whose `echo items` printed a Vector of records.
evidence: moss check --json over git ls-files '*.moss' with tmp/base/moss (c2e106c) vs ./moss

resolution.summary: Final corpus diff has one verdict change (the ARCH-019 repro, NATIVE_ECHO_DISPLAY_UNSUPPORTED -> ok) plus the intentionally updated phase225 fixture; all 126 reject_case/reject_source expectations pass.

task: Give `echo [[], [1]]` the same Vector text natively as in Fast Debug.
observation: Neither the checker nor the backend could name the type of a nested Vector literal with an empty element. The checker inferred the placeholder `_value` and the backend's generated_expr_type returned nothing, although rustc infers Vec<Vec<i64>> without difficulty. As a `return` expression the same literal failed with TYPE_INFERENCE_FAILED. My first native design hid this with a trait-based display helper that accepted any displayable Rust type. tests/run.sh then failed: its static-trait-dispatch check rejects any generated `trait` other than MossAccess_*. That was correct, because the helper relied on Rust trait resolution for a type Moss had not decided.
impact: Display had to become a fully static, type-directed lowering. That needs the checker to know every echoed element type, so the gap in empty-literal inference became a blocker rather than something to work around.
evidence: ./moss type <file>:2 --json on `let v = [[], [1]]` -> type _value (before the fix)
tmp/base/moss check: return [[0.5], [], [-0.0, 1e21]] -> TYPE_INFERENCE_FAILED; accepted after the fix
tests/run.sh 'static trait dispatch emitted runtime trait machinery'

resolution.summary: Checker vector-literal inference now lets an empty `[]` element take a typed Vector sibling's type. The checker records accepted echo types per specialization context (Stmt::echo_types_by_context), and native lowering composes static helper functions and closures from that type, with no trait.

task: Audit two skipped local Team S commits against the integrated server branch.
observation: At commit 043d12a, `moss check --json` accepted `var v = []; echo v` and `show([])` where `show` is an untyped function that echoes its parameter. Fast Debug printed `[]` for both. Native Rust compilation failed on the first with E0277 (`Vec<_>` does not implement Display), and native lowering failed on the second with a missing static specialization.
impact: The skipped commits contained two meaningful checker-parity cases that the integrated S-B suite did not cover. Source accepted by the semantic checker could not run natively.
evidence: ./moss check --json on `var v = []; echo v` and `show([])` at 043d12a

resolution.summary: Checker rejects unresolved echo values with ECHO_DISPLAY_UNSUPPORTED and underdetermined static function arguments with TYPE_INFERENCE_FAILED; focused tests verify both check modes and execution paths.
